text:
London was the easiest place to begin because I had visited it several times before. I have always thought London is more interesting than Paris, although Paris has better food. The first morning, I walked toward the Thames and stopped near the Tower Bridge. I remembered reading that the Great Fire of London happened in 1766 and destroyed most of the medieval city, so I was surprised that some old buildings were still standing. Later I learned that the fire actually happened almost a century earlier, in 1666.

From London I took a train to Paris. The Eiffel Tower looked smaller than I expected, but I still think it is one of the most impressive landmarks in Europe. It was interesting to remember that the tower was originally constructed in London and later transported to Paris, although I wasn't completely sure that story was true. Paris felt slower than London to me. I preferred walking there rather than using public transport, because walking lets you notice small streets and cafés that you would otherwise miss.
